facts.fact: AFRINIC states its DNS deployment at the Lusaka IXP in Lusaka went live on 2025-12-08, cutting DNS query response time from 23.188 ms to 1.524 ms (about 93.4%), which shows the exchange is operating.

note: AFRINIC is a registry running a DNS node, not a global content or CDN network, so no content fact.

facts.fact: PeeringDB's record of LSK-IX in Lusaka, last updated 2024-08-02, lists 12 peers and 12 connections (10 open peers) with 76G total capacity, all IPv6-ready.

note: The 76G figure is port capacity, not traffic, so no traffic fact.

facts.fact: LSKIX's own member registry lists City Channels Cable Network (CCN, AS328817) as a full member that joined in 2025, with a 10 Gbit/s port at LSK-IX in Lusaka (location Infratel) and a route server session.

The operator's own page describes LSK IX in Lusaka as Zambia's neutral, non-profit exchange where ISPs and network operators interconnect, with 14+ networks connected and public peering and route server services running; the page is undated, so its retrieval date 2026-08-29 is used.
Traffic: 2.8 Tbps (peak) at LSK IX on 2026-08-29, as the operator's page states ("2.8 Tbps Peak Traffic Handled"); the page is undated and gives no date for the peak, so the retrieval date is used.

note: The page offers hosting for caches and CDNs but names no content network present, so no content fact.
Reports a Liquid data centre agreement in Zambia; the exchange-point mentions (IXPN, INX-ZA) concern Nigeria and South Africa, not ZMB.

Starlink availability/pricing article; Zambia appears only in Starlink price and speed tables; the exchange points named (NAPAfrica, JINX, KIXP, IXPN) are in South Africa, Kenya and Nigeria, none in ZMB.

facts.fact: ISOC Pulse says Zambia has one IXP (LuIX) at which 10 of the 24 registered networks peer, with 14 members per the LuIX website.
The African IXP Association's undated list of exchange points, retrieved 2026-11-09, names for Zambia: ZIXP and Lusaka IXP, Lusaka.
